title: Category spread
prompt: Show each category with its cheapest price as lowest and highest price as highest, sorted by category.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT category, MIN(price) AS lowest, MAX(price) AS highest FROM products GROUP BY category ORDER BY category;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT category, MAX(price) AS lowest, MIN(price) AS highest FROM products GROUP BY category ORDER BY category;
SELECT category, MIN(price) AS lowest, MAX(price) AS highest FROM products ORDER BY category;

title: Active users per device
prompt: Show each device and the number of different users on it, as users.
solutions: SELECT device, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS users FROM sessions GROUP BY device;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT device, COUNT(*) AS users FROM sessions GROUP BY device;
SELECT device, COUNT(user_id) AS users FROM sessions GROUP BY device;

title: Busy students
prompt: Show the student_id of students with at least 3 enrolments.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (15, 7, 5, 70, '2024-autumn');

solutions: SELECT student_id FROM enrolments GROUP BY student_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT student_id FROM enrolments GROUP BY student_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 3;
SELECT student_id FROM enrolments GROUP BY student_id;

title: Bonus coverage
prompt: Show each department_id and the percentage of its staff with a bonus above 0, rounded to 1 decimal, as covered_pct.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT department_id, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN bonus > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 1) AS covered_pct FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT department_id, ROUND(COUNT(bonus) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 1) AS covered_pct FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;
SELECT department_id, SUM(CASE WHEN bonus > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS covered_pct FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;

title: Hottest day per city
prompt: Show each city and its highest temperature as hottest, hottest city first.
hints: Group, take the maximum, then sort.
solutions: SELECT city, MAX(temp_c) AS hottest FROM readings GROUP BY city ORDER BY hottest DESC;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT city, MIN(temp_c) AS hottest FROM readings GROUP BY city ORDER BY hottest DESC;
SELECT city, MAX(temp_c) AS hottest FROM readings GROUP BY city ORDER BY hottest;

title: Heavy orders
prompt: Show each order_id with more than 3 total units, and those units as units.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id HAVING SUM(quantity) > 3;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_items WHERE quantity > 3 GROUP BY order_id;
SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS units FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 3;

title: Hires per year
prompt: Show each hire year as year and how many people were hired as hires, in year order.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT strftime('%Y', hire_date) AS year, COUNT(*) AS hires FROM employees GROUP BY year ORDER BY year;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', hire_date) AS year, COUNT(*) AS hires FROM employees GROUP BY hire_date ORDER BY year;
SELECT hire_date AS year, COUNT(*) AS hires FROM employees GROUP BY hire_date ORDER BY year;

title: Maths or nothing
prompt: Show each term and the average grade rounded to 2 decimals as average, for course 1 only.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring'); UPDATE enrolments SET course_id = 1 WHERE id IN (11, 14); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (15, 8, 1, 62, '2024-spring'), (16, 7, 1, 63, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT term, ROUND(AVG(grade), 2) AS average FROM enrolments WHERE course_id = 1 GROUP BY term;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT term, ROUND(AVG(grade), 2) AS average FROM enrolments GROUP BY term;
SELECT term, AVG(grade) AS average FROM enrolments WHERE course_id = 1 GROUP BY term;

title: Contacts by city
prompt: Show each known city with its number of contacts as contacts. Leave out contacts with no city.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3');

solutions: SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS contacts FROM contacts WHERE city IS NOT NULL GROUP BY city;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS contacts FROM contacts GROUP BY city;
SELECT city, COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS contacts FROM contacts;

title: Longest day
prompt: Show the session_date with the most total minutes, and the total as total. Break ties with the earliest date.
hints: Group, sort on two columns, and limit.
solutions: SELECT session_date, SUM(minutes) AS total FROM sessions GROUP BY session_date ORDER BY total DESC, session_date LIMIT 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT session_date, MAX(minutes) AS total FROM sessions GROUP BY session_date ORDER BY total DESC, session_date LIMIT 1;
SELECT session_date, SUM(minutes) AS total FROM sessions GROUP BY session_date ORDER BY total DESC, session_date DESC LIMIT 1;
wrongSolutions.why: Breaks ties with the latest date
